question.problem:
The disjoint union ${A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2}⊔{A}_{3}$ of events ${A}_{1},{A}_{2},{A}_{3}$ covers the entire sample space. Compute $P({A}_{1}|B)$ given the following probabilities:

$$
\begin{aligned} & P(B|{A}_{1})=0, & P({A}_{1})=0.25 \\  & P(B|{A}_{2})=0.6, & P({A}_{2})=0.25 \\  & P(B|{A}_{3})=0.3, & P({A}_{3})=0.5\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
If the disjoint union ${A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2}⊔…⊔{A}_{n}$ covers the entire sample space, Bayes' theorem combined with the law of total probability gives us the following:

$$
P({A}_{k}|B)=\frac{P(B|{A}_{k})P({A}_{k})}{P(B)}=\frac{P(B|{A}_{k})P({A}_{k})}{{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}P(B|{A}_{i})P({A}_{i})}
$$

where $k=1,2,…,n.$

In our case, $n=3,$ and ${A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2}⊔{A}_{3}$ covers the entire sample space. Consequently, we have

$$
P({A}_{1})+P({A}_{2})+P({A}_{3})=0.25+0.25+0.5=1.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P({A}_{1}|B) & =\frac{P(B|{A}_{1})P({A}_{1})}{{\sum }_{i=1}^{3}P(B|{A}_{i})P({A}_{i})} \\  & =\frac{P(B|{A}_{1})P({A}_{1})}{P(B|{A}_{1})P({A}_{1})+P(B|{A}_{2})P({A}_{2})+P(B|{A}_{3})P({A}_{3})} \\  & =\frac{(0)(0.25)}{(0)(0.25)+(0.6)(0.25)+(0.3)(0.5)} \\  & =\frac{0}{0.3} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
